To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
adding on-screen text to an auditory narration of a scientific explanation facilitates comprehension, provided there is no other concurrent visual information.
the addition of text to the audio narration of a multimedia explanation can be beneficial for learning, but only when the text does not distract from the explanation.
verbal redundancy in multimedia learning is beneficial, provided that no concurrent visual material is present, and that this is due to the dual-processing nature of working memory.

the role of verbal redundancy in multimedia learning.
the question of when and how the addition of onscreen text facilitates the learning of a multimedia explanation.
the effects of adding on-screen text to a narrated multimedia presentation.

the addition of onscreen text to an explanation presented in the auditory modality is beneficial to learning when there is no concurrent visual material.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the addition of onscreen text facilitates learning when the words are presented simultaneously with the corresponding animation and when the words are not accompanied by any other visual information.
when the words are presented auditorily and on screen at the same time, they help each other to be processed, provided there is no other concurrent visual information.

the use of on-screen text can be a powerful means to enhance multimedia learning.
